title: RUNE 1h looks like it's coiling under resistance. Anyone else watching this?
author: FarInspector1873
selftext:
RUNE ran about 5% on Oct 15 (roughly 0.622 to 0.654). It has since spent around 20 hours moving sideways to slightly down in a tight, gently falling channel.

My notes:

* Volume spiked on the run-up, then dried up during the consolidation. That's the pattern you'd want to see for a bull flag.
* The upper line has been tested 6 times and the lower line 5 times. The range is clean, and it keeps narrowing.
* Price is now pressed against the top of the channel, around 0.651. The last several candles are small and sitting right on resistance.

A 1h close above about 0.652 would be the breakout trigger. The measured move from the pole would point to roughly 0.67-0.68. A drop below about 0.640 would invalidate the setup.

Caveats: the pole is only 5%, so the move is small, and 1h charts produce plenty of fakeouts. Breakouts also tend to need a volume pickup to hold, and I haven't seen that yet.

Am I reading this right, or is it just chop? I'm curious whether anyone has a bigger-picture level that matters here.

*Not financial advice, just sharing a chart.*

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body: six touches on the upper line usually means sellers are thinning out there, but a 1h channel drifting down for 20 hours can just as easily be distribution. I'd want the breakout candle on volume before calling it a flag.
